title: Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Agents: Benchmark Variation Using Inspect AI

original_idea.title: Prompt Injection in Tool-Using Agents: Benchmark Variation Using Inspect AI
original_idea.problem: Prompt injection attacks in tool-using agents can cause agents to take unsafe actions via malicious content in retrieved documents. Existing evals cover this sparsely.
original_idea.direction: Using Inspect AI's agent evaluation framework, construct 20–30 tasks where malicious instructions are embedded in simulated tool outputs (e.g., web search results, file contents). Measure whether 2–3 open-source models comply with injected instructions vs. their original task. Vary injection visibility (obvious vs. subtle) and severity (benign redirection vs. harmful action).
original_idea.why_it_matters: Prompt injection is a well-known but poorly benchmarked agentic risk. Inspect AI provides the infrastructure; what is missing is a focused safety-specific injection benchmark.
original_idea.relevant_context: Inspect AI (UK AISI, 100+ evals) is explicitly mentioned as a key tool. Agent Security Bench (ASB, ICLR 2025) covers some injection scenarios but in a complex multi-scenario format not suited for beginners.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Prompt injection is a critical agentic safety risk. A focused benchmark directly contributes to identifying vulnerable models and improving defenses. High practical relevance.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Requires learning Inspect AI framework and constructing agent evaluation tasks. Not trivial for beginners, though Inspect AI documentation is good. Mentor guidance essential.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Constructing 20-30 injection tasks with varied visibility and severity, plus setting up Inspect AI agent scaffolding, is substantial. Could be narrowed to 10-15 tasks for 30 hours.

novelty.reasoning: Multiple comprehensive benchmarks already exist for prompt injection in tool-using agents. Agent Security Bench (ASB, ICLR 2025) covers 27 attack types across 13 LLM backbones with attack success rates exceeding 84%. AgentHarm (ICLR 2025) evaluates 110 unique agentic behaviors across 11 harm categories using 104 tools. AgentDojo provides dynamic prompt injection evaluation for LLM agents. AgentDyn (arXiv 2602.03117) further addresses real-world complexity. The proposed Inspect AI variation adds a specific framework choice but the research question (measuring agent susceptibility to prompt injection in tool outputs) is well-addressed.
